newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Roth won't rule out rate cut - paper.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Roth won't rule out rate cut - paper.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) Vice-chairman Jean-Pierre Roth declined to rule out an interest rate cut if the stagnant Swiss economy does not start to recover or the recovery is very weak, a Swiss newspaper reported.
Asked by La Liberte if a rate cut was possible under these conditions, Roth said: "This is one variant. One cannot exclude it."
A SNB spokesman declined comment on the report, which appeared in the Fribourg paper's weekend editions.
Roth reiterated the SNB's forecast that gross domestic product would grow a real 0.5 percent in 1997.
The SNB switched to an expansionary monetary policy in 1995 to help spur the flagging economy and bring down the Swiss franc's exchange rate.
It last cut the discount rate by half a point to 1.00 on September 26, 1996, matching a record low maintained from February 1978 to November 1979.

SNB officials have repeatedly said they will keep policy generous until they see clear signs of an economic upturn, although they have also cited the danger of stoking inflationary pressure by leaving policy loose for too long.
